messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak from last week, we started seeing OOMs on AWQ-quantized LLMs with long contexts (6-8k). Repro on staging with dedicated 32GB A100 pool. Heap jumps ~4GB during KV write phase.

jon: ack. saw an alert earlier. is this only AWQ or GPTQ too?

maria: primarily AWQ so far. GPTQ models run but with higher latency; FP8 runs look inconsistent (sometimes upcast to fp16 on KV write).

kai: could be the kernel fallback path that forces a temporary upcast when an instruction isn't supported in FP8 for the write/store kernel. Do we have profiling traces?

maria: pasted a short perf snippet from the repro run (staging, batch=1, seq=8192):

```
2026-03-15 18:12:03.123 TRACE runtime.kernel_selector: selected kernel: attention_fp8_fused (fastpath)
2026-03-15 18:12:03.124 WARN runtime.kernel_selector: fallback to attention_fp16_store for kv_write (missing fused-store for this blocksize)
2026-03-15 18:12:03.130 INFO runtime.kv_cache: kv_write: dtype=fp8 -> temp_upcast=fp16 size=1.2GB
2026-03-15 18:12:03.140 ERROR runtime.allocator: OOM when allocating 1.1GB for kv_scratch
```

maria: note the mmap/alloc pattern — allocator tries to satisfy a large contiguous scratch allocation which spikes reserved memory and triggers OOM because we already have model params + activations pinned.

sophia: that aligns with the allocator-commit heuristic change we merged (deferred-free window shortened). We made the window smaller to reduce UAF risk, but it reduces reclaim headroom. Could be compounding.

jon: two possible short-term mitigations: 1) force kernel selector to prefer a slower in-place FP8 store (even if slightly slower) to avoid upcast; 2) add per-model KV dtype override so AWQ models always keep kv in fp8 and use an FP8-compatible store. Which is easier to ship to staging?

kai: I can patch the selector to prefer 'store_compatibility' over 'perf_score' for models flagged by eng-ml. Minimal change in selector heuristics: add weight for kv_store_supported flag. Patch should be safe to A/B.

maria: also we should avoid a large contiguous scratch alloc. Can we change workspace sizing to use chunked scratch buffers? Example fallback: allocate N x 128MB slices instead of one 1.1GB block. That would reduce fragmentation failure.

kai: yes — allocator can expose a 'slice_allocate' path. But that needs runtime kernel support for scatter-gather buffers (simple to add for kv_write case). I'll prototype.

sophia: long-term: re-evaluate deferred-free window revert + add a soft-reserve budget for kv writes when model is quantized. That keeps headroom for upcasts. Also we should surface per-model memory footprinter in Console so customers can see when their AWQ config would hit limits.

maria: for immediate triage on staging, here's a bisect plan:
- revert selector change on one node pool (A) -> confirm regression clears
- deploy kernel-selector patch that biases store_compatibility on pool (B) -> see if upcast disappears
- enable chunked scratch allocation on pool (C) -> check for OOM/noise
- run repro harness: `./tools/repro_run --model redwood-awq-30b --seq 8192 --batch 1 --iters 5`

jon: logging to help with verification: add these traces temporarily:
```
TRACE runtime.kv_cache: pre_write_reserve=(used=23.4GB reserved=24.7GB soft_reserve=0.5GB)
TRACE runtime.allocator: alloc_request(size=1153433600) -> try_slice=true -> slices=[128MB x 9] -> success
TRACE runtime.kernel_selector: chosen_store=fused_fp8_store (compat=true)
```

maria: infra-bot: can you spin a 3-node staging pool with A100-32GB and tag them as pool-A/B/C for the bisect?

infra-bot: Created pools: staging-pool-A (selector-revert), staging-pool-B (selector-bias), staging-pool-C (chunked-scratch). Images: runtime-v1.42. Tags: bisect-oom-2055.

kai: I pushed a draft selector patch to `eng-runtime/selector/bias-kv-store` — quick test indicates kv temp_upcast logs disappear. Patch is small, will make PR.

maria: pushed a small allocator change to `eng-runtime/allocator/chunked-scratch-proto` — experimental behind feature-flag `KV_CHUNKED_SCRATCH`.

jon: running repro against pool-B now. Will post results in ~20m.

(20 minutes later)

jon: quick results: pool-A (revert) -> no OOM, latency same as baseline; pool-B (selector-bias) -> no upcast observed, memory stable; pool-C (chunked) -> no OOM, slight perf hit (~4% tail latency increase) but stable.

maria: great. so immediate next steps:
- ship selector-bias as hotfix to production for AWQ models (safe toggle per-model)
- merge chunked scratch with opt-in FF for now (monitor perf)
- follow-up: add per-model KV dtype override and memory footprinter in Console

kai: will open PR for selector-bias, include tests that force fallback path and assert no temporary upcast.

sophia: I'll make a product ticket to spec Console footprinter + an API to pin KV dtype. Also add an eval to eng-ml to run AWQ long-context smoke.

maria: thanks team. we'll continue monitoring for FP8/GPTQ mixed-precision corner cases. If anyone sees regressions on other quant formats, ping here with repro and the `runtime.kernel_selector` trace. :thumbsup:

jon: added notes to the incident runbook: under 'quantization' -> 'kernel-fallback upcast' and mitigation checklist.

maria: closing loop once PRs merged and hotfix rolled.
